rapport_notes: Brianne is warm, patient, friendly, and handles customer questions with genuine helpfulness and zero defensiveness throughout.
process_discipline_notes: Rep asked 'do you have any questions for me' mid-Stage 3 (after pricing/estimate delivered) and moved directly into answering without holding silence for customer response — no pause gap.

evidence_quotes.agenda: Rep asked: 'do you have any questions or concerns specific me about this move that you'd like answered on the call?' — but only after briefly probing the booking details, not at the very start of discovery.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Desk concern: 'Absolutely that is actually included in our hourly rate, so there's no extra charge for any disassemble or reassembly of items.' Then: 'All shape desk that needs to be disassembled Ma. Any item, other items that needs special care.' Bookcase follow-up: 'Is that something that you assembled inside?' → 'Alright, definitely can take care of that for you.' Customer raised additional concerns (mattress, bed frame, washer/dryer) and rep followed up on each with clarifying questions (Purple mattress, basic frame, unhooking appliances). Full two-layer follow-up across all concerns.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Rep delivered: (1) 'estimate your move definitely to fall within that two and a half to three and a half hour range' (anchor/range + personalization) + 'Once we go over that minimum the time is prorated in 215 minute increments' (beats-it-pay-less). (2) 'the most important [factor] is how well prepared you are when you get there...consolidating things in the boxes...would really help keep the time down' (self-prep tip). (3) No explicit 'does that feel fair?' asked or held with silence. (4) No 'we commit to the rate / 100k moves' framing. (5) 'estimate is a window' implied via the range language but never explicitly named as such.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_damage_coverage: Rep said: 'We do have our no worries damage coverage. Our free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate that provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.' — delivered in Stage 2 as part of takeaway, not raised by customer in Stage 1, so credit lands in Stage 2.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_meet_your_mover: Rep said: 'A few days before your move, you'll receive and meet your mover email introducing them to you helping ease detention of strangers arriving at your front door.' — also delivered in Stage 2 as part of takeaway, not answered to a Stage 1 concern.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Rep said: 'we also do have our on time guarantee we value your time. So, if we can't make it in the time window that we arrange, we may daly start discounting money of your final bill' — delivered in Stage 2.
evidence_quotes.communication: Rep said: 'they will give you a call the day before to confirm the move and then they will call you the morning of to let you know they're on their way' — delivered at the very end of Stage 3, after pricing, not in Stage 2 takeaway.
evidence_quotes.close: Rep said: 'they will see you on Tuesday September 15th' and then transitioned to small talk ('Have a good rest of your day. Thank you for your time'). No rate-lock line ('your rate locks when you book'). No explicit ask ('would you like our help with your move?'). Call ends with goodbye.

top_strength: Brianne demonstrated excellent two-layer follow-up on customer concerns, remaining patient and thorough through multiple disassembly, mattress, and appliance questions without rushing or dismissing any of them.
coaching_note: Add a time-boxed framing ('should take about X minutes, then I'll build you an accurate quote') at the very start of discovery; close with both a rate-lock mention and an explicit ask for the booking; and hold silence after open-ended questions like 'does that feel fair?' to let the customer respond without immediate re-pitch.
